{{神社 |名称= 久具都比賣神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=[[File:Kugutsuhime-jinja.jpg|270px]] |所在地 = [[三重県]][[度会郡]][[度会町]]上久具[[小字|字]]久具都裏211 |緯度度 = 34 | 緯度分 = 25 | 緯度秒 = 57.7 |経度度 = 136 |経度分 = 36 | 経度秒 = 44.9 |地図= Japan Mie |祭神= 久具都比女命
久具都比古命
御前神 |社格= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}（小）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}}摂社 |創建= [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿= [[神明造]] |別名= クグツヒメさん |札所等= |例祭= |神事= [[神嘗祭]] }} '''Kugutsuhime Shrine''' (久具都比賣神社) is a {{ill|sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sessha|qq=}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} ({{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}) (Inner Shrine). It was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}{{ill|Ise Culture Publishing|ja|伊勢文化舎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Culture Publishing|qq=}} (2008): p.72{{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|qq=}} (2013): p.66. The shrine is located along the [[Miya River (Mie)]] and part of the shrine grounds is occasionally subject to flooding{{ill|Shikinaisha Research Association|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft研究会|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha Research Association|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (1990): p.289. == Overview == {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}} {{ill|Tōai District|ja|度会郡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōai District|qq=}} {{ill|Tōai Town|ja|度会町|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōai Town|qq=}} Kamikugu, in the small area ({{ill|koaza|ja|小字|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/koaza|qq=}}) of Kugutsu-uraji, is the location of this shrine. It is the only shrine affiliated with the 【神宮摂社】 (Shingū Sessha) in Tōai Town.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |title=伊勢神宮御萱場と一之瀬川流域めぐり旅 |publisher=度会町役場総務課行政係・財政係 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-19 |accessdate=2013-11-25 |archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1125-2141-54/www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |archivedate=2013-11-25}} Among the facilities related to {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}, besides Kugutsuhime Shrine, there is also the Shingū Mikayaba located at the river’s mouth. It is Ranked 21st among the 27 subsidiary shrines (摂社) of the inner shrine.宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：9 - 11ページ The {{ill|shaden|ja|社殿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shaden|qq=}} is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} style with a {{ill|itafuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/itafuki|qq=}} roof, and is enclosed by a single layer of {{ill|tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tamagaki|qq=}}.式内社研究会 編（1990）：292ページ Its dimensions are approximately 6 shaku wide (≒1.82 m), 4 shaku deep (≒1.21 m), and 7 shaku 8 sun high (≒2.36 m). The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,004 {{ill|m²|ja|平方メートル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/m²|qq=}}. The northern side of the shrine grounds adjoins the {{ill|Miyagawa|ja|宮川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyagawa|qq=}}. When the river swells, the area around the shrine may be flooded. == 社名 == The name “Kugu” (久具) is believed to be derived from a 【地名】 (place name), although the origin of the place name “Kugu” is unknown. The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' refers to the shrine as “Kugutsuhime Shrine” (久々都比賣神社), the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'' as “Kugu Shrine” (久具神社), and the ''{{ill|Yamato Himen Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Himen Seiki|qq=}}'' as “Kugu-sha” (久求社). Locals affectionately call it “Kugutsu Hime-san”. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}} The deities enshrined here are {{ill|Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比女命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比古命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, and {{ill|Mimae-no-Kami|ja|御前神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimae-no-Kami|qq=}}. They are regarded as the water deity—who irrigates the land of Kugu—and as a god of the five grains. This deity is identified as a child of {{ill|Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|ja|大水上命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was venerated locally as a god of water and rice cultivation even before {{ill|Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto|qq=}} toured Ise. Various ancient texts such as ''{{ill|Sessessha Kokon Shidai|ja|摂末社古今次第|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sessessha Kokon Shidai|qq=}}'' confirm the names of Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto and Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, but the name of a third deity is not clearly stated.式内社研究会 編（1990）：290ページ According to tradition, these two deities appeared to greet Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto when she visited the land of Kugu. In ''{{ill|Daijingu Gishikikai|ja|大神宮儀式解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijingu Gishikikai|qq=}}'', the third deity is interpreted as the deity of the former shrine (i.e., Mimae-no-Kami), and the ''{{ill|Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|ja|神三郡神社参詣記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|qq=}}'' refers to it as “Yamajin” (mountain god). == History == According to tradition, when Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto traveled down the {{ill|Ichinose River|ja|一之瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinose River|qq=}}, she was met by Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, and Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto declared that the land was “Kugu Kono,” leading Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto to establish “Kugu-sha”. More definitively, by the definition of subsidiary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, the creation of this shrine must have occurred before the establishment of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in the 5th year of the {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} era (927 AD).伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：22ページ It is also recorded in the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'', indicating that it existed before the 23rd year of the {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enryaku|qq=}} era (804 AD). The ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'' stipulates that if the shrine is destroyed, it should be rebuilt with proper taxation, and the ''Daijingu Shiki'' states that the shrine priest ({{ill|guji|ja|宮司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guji|qq=}}) is responsible for its repair. Furthermore, according to the ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'', there were once three main shrine buildings (正殿三宇) arranged side by side. During the medieval period, the shrine buildings fell into disrepair and even the shrine grounds became unidentifiable. In the 3rd year of the {{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanbun|qq=}} era, on September 8 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: October 8, 1663), the great shrine priest {{ill|Kawabe Seichō|ja|河邊精長|lt=Kawabe Seichō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Seichō|qq=}} (also known as Ōnakomi Seichō) made efforts to restore the shrine grounds, and on December 12 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: January 10, 1664) the relocation ceremony (遷御) was conducted. At that time, the three shrine buildings that had existed in ancient times were consolidated into one. Later, on October 7 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: November 14, 1692) the shrine building was reconstructed, and the relocation ceremony was carried out on February 18 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: March 13, 1694). According to the ''式内社調査報告'', the restored shrine grounds are undoubtedly the original site. The shrine building was rebuilt in September 1917 (Taishō 6)宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：11ページ and again in November 1955 (Shōwa 30), and a major repair was carried out in May 1979 (Shōwa 54). == Rites == In February, the {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinensai|qq=}} is held; in June and December, the {{ill|Getsusai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Getsusai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} is performed; in October, the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}} is conducted; and in November, the {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niinamesai|qq=}} is held in front of the shrine building, while the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January) is observed with remote worship at the Gojōden of the Imperial Grand Shrine.式内社研究会 編（1990）：291ページ A local custom called “Gosaimairi” (御祭まいり) is also practiced.櫻井（1991）：294ページ This involves many residents visiting the shrine on Lunisolar June 17 and Lunisolar September 17 (the original date of the Kannamesai before the calendar reform). == 植物相 == According to a survey conducted in 1980 (Shōwa 55), the major trees on the grounds are {{ill|Sugi|ja|スギ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugi|qq=}}, {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki|qq=}}, while the smaller trees consist of {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=evergreen broadleaf trees|ja|常緑広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}} and {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=deciduous broadleaf trees|ja|落葉広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}}. Moss grows along the {{ill|sandō|ja|参道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sandō|qq=}}. == 上久具の渡しと久具都比売橋 == To the east of {{ill|Kugutsuhime Shrine|ja|久具都比賣神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime Shrine|qq=}}, there is the site of a ferry known as “Kamikugu no Watashi” (上久具の渡し) which operated for approximately 90 years.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：70 - 71ページ The Kamikugu ferry connected Kamikugu on both banks of the Miyagawa (upper Kugu) and Tanahashi until March 1994 (Heisei 6), facilitating the movement of people and goods.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71 - 72ページ In 1994 (Heisei 6), the construction of the Kugutsuhime Bridge resulted in the termination of the Kamikugu ferry service, which had been the last operating ferry in Mie Prefecture. Due to frequent fluctuations in the river’s water level, the Kamikugu ferry often caused difficulties for its users. As of 2013 (Heisei 25), clear remnants of the ferry landing remain on the Kamikugu side, and traces of a staircase serving as a school route can also be seen on the opposite Tanahashi side. == 交通 == ;公共交通 * From the South Exit of {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Station|qq=}} (JR side) on the {{ill|Sangu Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangu Line|qq=}} of {{ill|JR (Tokai Passenger Railway)|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR (Tokai Passenger Railway)|qq=}}, or the {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|lt=Yamada Line|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}} of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}}, take the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} route bus bound for either {{ill|Shimesasu|ja|注連指|lt=Shimesasu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimesasu|qq=}} or {{ill|Uedaguchi|ja|上田口|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uedaguchi|qq=}}, ride for approximately 30 minutes, alight at the {{ill|Dōkai Housing Complex|ja|度会団地前|lt=Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=}} bus stop, then walk for about 5 minutes.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kankomie.or.jp/spot/detail_8513.html |title=久具都比売神社（くぐつひめじんじゃ）の観光施設・周辺情報 - 観光三重 |publisher=三重県観光連盟 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-07 |accessdate=2013-11-25}} The bus runs roughly once per hour.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71ページ ;自家用車 * From {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Expressway|qq=}} at {{ill|Tamakishima Interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|lt=Tamakishima IC|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamakishima Interchange|qq=}}, head south on {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|ja|三重県道65号度会玉城線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|qq=}} (Sunny Road) for about 10 minutes. * From {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Station|qq=}}, via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|ja|三重県道38号伊勢大宮線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|qq=}}, approximately 12.5 {{ill|km|ja|キロメートル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/km|qq=}}. '''Kugutsuhime Shrine''' (久具都比売神社) == References == {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * [[伊勢文化舎]] 編『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、伊勢文化舎、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 == See Also == * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of 125 Shrines of Ise|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=}} * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=}} * [[ヒメヒコ制]] == External Links == {{ external media | align = | width = 230px | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image1 = [http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/images/shrine/area05/area05_03.jpg 久具都比賣神社] }} * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m06/0609.html 久具都比賣神社（くぐつひめじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [http://www.kirari1000.com/www.kirari1000.com.base_data.base_data.phpQkirari_cd=04648.html 久具都比売神社] - [[伊勢志摩きらり千選]]（財団法人伊勢志摩国立公園協会） : {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{translated page|ja|久具都比売神社|version=57871040|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Setsumatsusha]] [[Category:Shinto_shrines_in_Mie_Prefecture]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] }} [[ja:久具都比売神社]] [[ja:久具都比賣神社]] [[sn:Kugutsuhime Shrine]] [[en:Kugutsuhime Shrine]] [[sn:ugutsuhime Shrine]]

{{神社 |名称= 久具都比賣神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=[[File:Kugutsuhime-jinja.jpg|270px]] |所在地 = [[三重県]][[度会郡]][[度会町]]上久具[[小字|字]]久具都裏211 |緯度度 = 34 | 緯度分 = 25 | 緯度秒 = 57.7 |経度度 = 136 |経度分 = 36 | 経度秒 = 44.9 |地図= Japan Mie |祭神= 久具都比女命
久具都比古命
御前神 |社格= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}（小）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}}摂社 |創建= [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿= [[神明造]] |別名= クグツヒメさん |札所等= |例祭= |神事= [[神嘗祭]] }} '''Kugutsuhime Shrine''' (久具都比賣神社) is a {{ill|sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sessha|qq=}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} ({{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}) (Inner Shrine). It was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=}}{{ill|Ise Culture Publishing|ja|伊勢文化舎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Culture Publishing|qq=}} (2008): p.72{{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|qq=}} (2013): p.66. The shrine is located along the [[Miya River (Mie)]] and part of the shrine grounds is occasionally subject to flooding{{ill|Shikinaisha Research Association|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft研究会|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha Research Association|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (1990): p.289. == Overview == {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}} {{ill|Tōai District|ja|度会郡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōai District|qq=}} {{ill|Tōai Town|ja|度会町|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōai Town|qq=}} Kamikugu, in the small area ({{ill|koaza|ja|小字|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/koaza|qq=}}) of Kugutsu-uraji, is the location of this shrine. It is the only shrine affiliated with the 【神宮摂社】 (Shingū Sessha) in Tōai Town.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |title=伊勢神宮御萱場と一之瀬川流域めぐり旅 |publisher=度会町役場総務課行政係・財政係 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-19 |accessdate=2013-11-25 |archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1125-2141-54/www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |archivedate=2013-11-25}} Among the facilities related to {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}, besides Kugutsuhime Shrine, there is also the Shingū Mikayaba located at the river’s mouth. It is Ranked 21st among the 27 subsidiary shrines (摂社) of the inner shrine.宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：9 - 11ページ The {{ill|shaden|ja|社殿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shaden|qq=}} is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} style with a {{ill|itafuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/itafuki|qq=}} roof, and is enclosed by a single layer of {{ill|tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tamagaki|qq=}}.式内社研究会 編（1990）：292ページ Its dimensions are approximately 6 shaku wide (≒1.82 m), 4 shaku deep (≒1.21 m), and 7 shaku 8 sun high (≒2.36 m). The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,004 {{ill|m²|ja|平方メートル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/m²|qq=}}. The northern side of the shrine grounds adjoins the {{ill|Miyagawa|ja|宮川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyagawa|qq=}}. When the river swells, the area around the shrine may be flooded. == 社名 == The name “Kugu” (久具) is believed to be derived from a 【地名】 (place name), although the origin of the place name “Kugu” is unknown. The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' refers to the shrine as “Kugutsuhime Shrine” (久々都比賣神社), the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'' as “Kugu Shrine” (久具神社), and the ''{{ill|Yamato Himen Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Himen Seiki|qq=}}'' as “Kugu-sha” (久求社). Locals affectionately call it “Kugutsu Hime-san”. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}} The deities enshrined here are {{ill|Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比女命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比古命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, and {{ill|Mimae-no-Kami|ja|御前神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimae-no-Kami|qq=}}. They are regarded as the water deity—who irrigates the land of Kugu—and as a god of the five grains. This deity is identified as a child of {{ill|Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|ja|大水上命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was venerated locally as a god of water and rice cultivation even before {{ill|Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto|qq=}} toured Ise. Various ancient texts such as ''{{ill|Sessessha Kokon Shidai|ja|摂末社古今次第|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sessessha Kokon Shidai|qq=}}'' confirm the names of Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto and Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, but the name of a third deity is not clearly stated.式内社研究会 編（1990）：290ページ According to tradition, these two deities appeared to greet Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto when she visited the land of Kugu. In ''{{ill|Daijingu Gishikikai|ja|大神宮儀式解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijingu Gishikikai|qq=}}'', the third deity is interpreted as the deity of the former shrine (i.e., Mimae-no-Kami), and the ''{{ill|Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|ja|神三郡神社参詣記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|qq=}}'' refers to it as “Yamajin” (mountain god). == History == According to tradition, when Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto traveled down the {{ill|Ichinose River|ja|一之瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinose River|qq=}}, she was met by Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, and Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto declared that the land was “Kugu Kono,” leading Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto to establish “Kugu-sha”. More definitively, by the definition of subsidiary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, the creation of this shrine must have occurred before the establishment of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in the 5th year of the {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} era (927 AD).伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：22ページ It is also recorded in the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'', indicating that it existed before the 23rd year of the {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enryaku|qq=}} era (804 AD). The ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'' stipulates that if the shrine is destroyed, it should be rebuilt with proper taxation, and the ''Daijingu Shiki'' states that the shrine priest ({{ill|guji|ja|宮司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guji|qq=}}) is responsible for its repair. Furthermore, according to the ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'', there were once three main shrine buildings (正殿三宇) arranged side by side. During the medieval period, the shrine buildings fell into disrepair and even the shrine grounds became unidentifiable. In the 3rd year of the {{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanbun|qq=}} era, on September 8 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: October 8, 1663), the great shrine priest {{ill|Kawabe Seichō|ja|河邊精長|lt=Kawabe Seichō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Seichō|qq=}} (also known as Ōnakomi Seichō) made efforts to restore the shrine grounds, and on December 12 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: January 10, 1664) the relocation ceremony (遷御) was conducted. At that time, the three shrine buildings that had existed in ancient times were consolidated into one. Later, on October 7 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: November 14, 1692) the shrine building was reconstructed, and the relocation ceremony was carried out on February 18 (old calendar) ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar|2=ja|3=グレゴリオ暦|4=fr|5=Calendrier grégorien|6=de|7=Gregorianischer Kalender|8=tl|9=Kalendaryong Gregoryano|10=ru|11=Григорианский календарь|ja|グレゴリオ暦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Gregorian calendar|qq=}}: March 13, 1694). According to the ''式内社調査報告'', the restored shrine grounds are undoubtedly the original site. The shrine building was rebuilt in September 1917 (Taishō 6)宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：11ページ and again in November 1955 (Shōwa 30), and a major repair was carried out in May 1979 (Shōwa 54). == Rites == In February, the {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinensai|qq=}} is held; in June and December, the {{ill|Getsusai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Getsusai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} is performed; in October, the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}} is conducted; and in November, the {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niinamesai|qq=}} is held in front of the shrine building, while the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January) is observed with remote worship at the Gojōden of the Imperial Grand Shrine.式内社研究会 編（1990）：291ページ A local custom called “Gosaimairi” (御祭まいり) is also practiced.櫻井（1991）：294ページ This involves many residents visiting the shrine on Lunisolar June 17 and Lunisolar September 17 (the original date of the Kannamesai before the calendar reform). == 植物相 == According to a survey conducted in 1980 (Shōwa 55), the major trees on the grounds are {{ill|Sugi|ja|スギ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugi|qq=}}, {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinoki|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki|qq=}}, while the smaller trees consist of {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=evergreen broadleaf trees|ja|常緑広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}} and {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=deciduous broadleaf trees|ja|落葉広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}}. Moss grows along the {{ill|sandō|ja|参道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sandō|qq=}}. == 上久具の渡しと久具都比売橋 == To the east of {{ill|Kugutsuhime Shrine|ja|久具都比賣神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime Shrine|qq=}}, there is the site of a ferry known as “Kamikugu no Watashi” (上久具の渡し) which operated for approximately 90 years.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：70 - 71ページ The Kamikugu ferry connected Kamikugu on both banks of the Miyagawa (upper Kugu) and Tanahashi until March 1994 (Heisei 6), facilitating the movement of people and goods.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71 - 72ページ In 1994 (Heisei 6), the construction of the Kugutsuhime Bridge resulted in the termination of the Kamikugu ferry service, which had been the last operating ferry in Mie Prefecture. Due to frequent fluctuations in the river’s water level, the Kamikugu ferry often caused difficulties for its users. As of 2013 (Heisei 25), clear remnants of the ferry landing remain on the Kamikugu side, and traces of a staircase serving as a school route can also be seen on the opposite Tanahashi side. == 交通 == ;公共交通 * From the South Exit of {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Station|qq=}} (JR side) on the {{ill|Sangu Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangu Line|qq=}} of {{ill|JR (Tokai Passenger Railway)|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR (Tokai Passenger Railway)|qq=}}, or the {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線|lt=Yamada Line|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Line|qq=}} of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}}, take the {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}} route bus bound for either {{ill|Shimesasu|ja|注連指|lt=Shimesasu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimesasu|qq=}} or {{ill|Uedaguchi|ja|上田口|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uedaguchi|qq=}}, ride for approximately 30 minutes, alight at the {{ill|Dōkai Housing Complex|ja|度会団地前|lt=Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=}} bus stop, then walk for about 5 minutes.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kankomie.or.jp/spot/detail_8513.html |title=久具都比売神社（くぐつひめじんじゃ）の観光施設・周辺情報 - 観光三重 |publisher=三重県観光連盟 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-07 |accessdate=2013-11-25}} The bus runs roughly once per hour.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71ページ ;自家用車 * From {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Expressway|qq=}} at {{ill|Tamakishima Interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|lt=Tamakishima IC|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamakishima Interchange|qq=}}, head south on {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|ja|三重県道65号度会玉城線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|qq=}} (Sunny Road) for about 10 minutes. * From {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Station|qq=}}, via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|ja|三重県道38号伊勢大宮線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|qq=}}, approximately 12.5 {{ill|km|ja|キロメートル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/km|qq=}}. '''Kugutsuhime Shrine''' (久具都比売神社) == References == {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * [[伊勢文化舎]] 編『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、伊勢文化舎、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. {{神社 |名称= 久具都比賣神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=[[File:Kugutsuhime-jinja.jpg|270px]] |所在地 = [[三重県]][[度会郡]][[度会町]]上久具[[小字|字]]久具都裏211 |緯度度 = 34 | 緯度分 = 25 | 緯度秒 = 57.7 |経度度 = 136 |経度分 = 36 | 経度秒 = 44.9 |地図= Japan Mie |祭神= 久具都比女命
久具都比古命
御前神 |社格= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}（小）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}}摂社 |創建= [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿= [[神明造]] |別名= クグツヒメさん |札所等= |例祭= |神事= [[神嘗祭]] }} '''Kugutsuhime Shrine''' (久具都比賣神社) is a {{ill|sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sessha|qq=}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} ([[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]) (Inner Shrine). It was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]]{{ill|Ise Culture Publishing|ja|伊勢文化舎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Culture Publishing|qq=}} (2008): p.72{{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|qq=}} (2013): p.66. The shrine is located along the [[Miya River (Mie)]] and part of the shrine grounds is occasionally subject to flooding{{ill|Shikinaisha Research Association|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft研究会|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha Research Association|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (1990): p.289. == Overview == [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]] [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Tōai District]] [[:en:Watarai|Tōai Town]] Kamikugu, in the small area ({{ill|koaza|ja|小字|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/koaza|qq=}}) of Kugutsu-uraji, is the location of this shrine. It is the only shrine affiliated with the 【神宮摂社】 (Shingū Sessha) in Tōai Town.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |title=伊勢神宮御萱場と一之瀬川流域めぐり旅 |publisher=度会町役場総務課行政係・財政係 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-19 |accessdate=2013-11-25 |archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1125-2141-54/www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |archivedate=2013-11-25}} Among the facilities related to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]], besides Kugutsuhime Shrine, there is also the Shingū Mikayaba located at the river’s mouth. It is Ranked 21st among the 27 subsidiary shrines (摂社) of the inner shrine.宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：9 - 11ページ The {{ill|shaden|ja|社殿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shaden|qq=}} is constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style with a {{ill|itafuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/itafuki|qq=}} roof, and is enclosed by a single layer of [[:en:Tamagaki|tamagaki]].式内社研究会 編（1990）：292ページ Its dimensions are approximately 6 shaku wide (≒1.82 m), 4 shaku deep (≒1.21 m), and 7 shaku 8 sun high (≒2.36 m). The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,004 [[:en:Square metre|m²]]. The northern side of the shrine grounds adjoins the [[:en:Miyagawa|Miyagawa]]. When the river swells, the area around the shrine may be flooded. == 社名 == The name “Kugu” (久具) is believed to be derived from a 【地名】 (place name), although the origin of the place name “Kugu” is unknown. The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' refers to the shrine as “Kugutsuhime Shrine” (久々都比賣神社), the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'' as “Kugu Shrine” (久具神社), and the ''{{ill|Yamato Himen Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Himen Seiki|qq=}}'' as “Kugu-sha” (久求社). Locals affectionately call it “Kugutsu Hime-san”. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}} The deities enshrined here are {{ill|Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比女命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比古命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, and {{ill|Mimae-no-Kami|ja|御前神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimae-no-Kami|qq=}}. They are regarded as the water deity—who irrigates the land of Kugu—and as a god of the five grains. This deity is identified as a child of {{ill|Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|ja|大水上命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was venerated locally as a god of water and rice cultivation even before [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto]] toured Ise. Various ancient texts such as ''{{ill|Sessessha Kokon Shidai|ja|摂末社古今次第|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sessessha Kokon Shidai|qq=}}'' confirm the names of Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto and Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, but the name of a third deity is not clearly stated.式内社研究会 編（1990）：290ページ According to tradition, these two deities appeared to greet Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto when she visited the land of Kugu. In ''{{ill|Daijingu Gishikikai|ja|大神宮儀式解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijingu Gishikikai|qq=}}'', the third deity is interpreted as the deity of the former shrine (i.e., Mimae-no-Kami), and the ''{{ill|Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|ja|神三郡神社参詣記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|qq=}}'' refers to it as “Yamajin” (mountain god). == History == According to tradition, when Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto traveled down the {{ill|Ichinose River|ja|一之瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinose River|qq=}}, she was met by Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, and Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto declared that the land was “Kugu Kono,” leading Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto to establish “Kugu-sha”. More definitively, by the definition of subsidiary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, the creation of this shrine must have occurred before the establishment of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in the 5th year of the {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} era (927 AD).伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：22ページ It is also recorded in the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'', indicating that it existed before the 23rd year of the [[:en:Enryaku|Enryaku]] era (804 AD). The ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'' stipulates that if the shrine is destroyed, it should be rebuilt with proper taxation, and the ''Daijingu Shiki'' states that the shrine priest ({{ill|guji|ja|宮司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guji|qq=}}) is responsible for its repair. Furthermore, according to the ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'', there were once three main shrine buildings (正殿三宇) arranged side by side. During the medieval period, the shrine buildings fell into disrepair and even the shrine grounds became unidentifiable. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Kanbun (era)|Kanbun]] era, on September 8 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: October 8, 1663), the great shrine priest {{ill|Kawabe Seichō|ja|河邊精長|lt=Kawabe Seichō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Seichō|qq=}} (also known as Ōnakomi Seichō) made efforts to restore the shrine grounds, and on December 12 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: January 10, 1664) the relocation ceremony (遷御) was conducted. At that time, the three shrine buildings that had existed in ancient times were consolidated into one. Later, on October 7 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: November 14, 1692) the shrine building was reconstructed, and the relocation ceremony was carried out on February 18 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: March 13, 1694). According to the ''式内社調査報告'', the restored shrine grounds are undoubtedly the original site. The shrine building was rebuilt in September 1917 (Taishō 6)宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：11ページ and again in November 1955 (Shōwa 30), and a major repair was carried out in May 1979 (Shōwa 54). == Rites == In February, the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinensai]] is held; in June and December, the {{ill|Getsusai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Getsusai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} is performed; in October, the [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]] is conducted; and in November, the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]] is held in front of the shrine building, while the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January) is observed with remote worship at the Gojōden of the Imperial Grand Shrine.式内社研究会 編（1990）：291ページ A local custom called “Gosaimairi” (御祭まいり) is also practiced.櫻井（1991）：294ページ This involves many residents visiting the shrine on Lunisolar June 17 and Lunisolar September 17 (the original date of the Kannamesai before the calendar reform). == 植物相 == According to a survey conducted in 1980 (Shōwa 55), the major trees on the grounds are [[:en:Cryptomeria|Sugi]], [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], and [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Kusunoki]], while the smaller trees consist of {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=evergreen broadleaf trees|ja|常緑広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}} and {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=deciduous broadleaf trees|ja|落葉広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}}. Moss grows along the [[:en:Sandō|sandō]]. == 上久具の渡しと久具都比売橋 == To the east of {{ill|Kugutsuhime Shrine|ja|久具都比賣神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime Shrine|qq=}}, there is the site of a ferry known as “Kamikugu no Watashi” (上久具の渡し) which operated for approximately 90 years.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：70 - 71ページ The Kamikugu ferry connected Kamikugu on both banks of the Miyagawa (upper Kugu) and Tanahashi until March 1994 (Heisei 6), facilitating the movement of people and goods.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71 - 72ページ In 1994 (Heisei 6), the construction of the Kugutsuhime Bridge resulted in the termination of the Kamikugu ferry service, which had been the last operating ferry in Mie Prefecture. Due to frequent fluctuations in the river’s water level, the Kamikugu ferry often caused difficulties for its users. As of 2013 (Heisei 25), clear remnants of the ferry landing remain on the Kamikugu side, and traces of a staircase serving as a school route can also be seen on the opposite Tanahashi side. == 交通 == ;公共交通 * From the South Exit of [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise City Station]] (JR side) on the [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangu Line]] of [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR (Tokai Passenger Railway)]], or the [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]] of [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]], take the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] route bus bound for either {{ill|Shimesasu|ja|注連指|lt=Shimesasu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimesasu|qq=}} or {{ill|Uedaguchi|ja|上田口|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uedaguchi|qq=}}, ride for approximately 30 minutes, alight at the {{ill|Dōkai Housing Complex|ja|度会団地前|lt=Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=}} bus stop, then walk for about 5 minutes.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kankomie.or.jp/spot/detail_8513.html |title=久具都比売神社（くぐつひめじんじゃ）の観光施設・周辺情報 - 観光三重 |publisher=三重県観光連盟 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-07 |accessdate=2013-11-25}} The bus runs roughly once per hour.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71ページ ;自家用車 * From [[:en:Ise Expressway|Ise Expressway]] at {{ill|Tamakishima Interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|lt=Tamakishima IC|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamakishima Interchange|qq=}}, head south on {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|ja|三重県道65号度会玉城線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|qq=}} (Sunny Road) for about 10 minutes. * From [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise City Station]], via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|ja|三重県道38号伊勢大宮線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|qq=}}, approximately 12.5 [[:en:Kilometre|km]]. {{神社 |名称= 久具都比賣神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=[[File:Kugutsuhime-jinja.jpg|270px]] |所在地 = [[三重県]][[度会郡]][[度会町]]上久具[[小字|字]]久具都裏211 |緯度度 = 34 | 緯度分 = 25 | 緯度秒 = 57.7 |経度度 = 136 |経度分 = 36 | 経度秒 = 44.9 |地図= Japan Mie |祭神= 久具都比女命
久具都比古命
御前神 |社格= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}（小）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}}摂社 |創建= [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿= [[神明造]] |別名= クグツヒメさん |札所等= |例祭= |神事= [[神嘗祭]] }} '''Kugutsuhime Shrine''' (久具都比賣神社) is a {{ill|sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sessha|qq=}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}} ([[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]) (Inner Shrine). It was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]]{{ill|Ise Culture Publishing|ja|伊勢文化舎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Culture Publishing|qq=}} (2008): p.72{{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|qq=}} (2013): p.66. The shrine is located along the [[Miya River (Mie)]] and part of the shrine grounds is occasionally subject to flooding{{ill|Shikinaisha Research Association|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft研究会|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha Research Association|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (1990): p.289. == Overview == [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]] [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Tōai District]] [[:en:Watarai|Tōai Town]] Kamikugu, in the small area ({{ill|koaza|ja|小字|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/koaza|qq=}}) of Kugutsu-uraji, is the location of this shrine. It is the only shrine affiliated with the 【神宮摂社】 (Shingū Sessha) in Tōai Town.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |title=伊勢神宮御萱場と一之瀬川流域めぐり旅 |publisher=度会町役場総務課行政係・財政係 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-19 |accessdate=2013-11-25 |archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1125-2141-54/www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |archivedate=2013-11-25}} Among the facilities related to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]], besides Kugutsuhime Shrine, there is also the Shingū Mikayaba located at the river’s mouth. It is Ranked 21st among the 27 subsidiary shrines (摂社) of the inner shrine.宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：9 - 11ページ The {{ill|shaden|ja|社殿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shaden|qq=}} is constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style with a {{ill|itafuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/itafuki|qq=}} roof, and is enclosed by a single layer of [[:en:Tamagaki|tamagaki]].式内社研究会 編（1990）：292ページ Its dimensions are approximately 6 shaku wide (≒1.82 m), 4 shaku deep (≒1.21 m), and 7 shaku 8 sun high (≒2.36 m). The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,004 [[:en:Square metre|m²]]. The northern side of the shrine grounds adjoins the [[:en:Miyagawa|Miyagawa]]. When the river swells, the area around the shrine may be flooded. == 社名 == The name “Kugu” (久具) is believed to be derived from a 【地名】 (place name), although the origin of the place name “Kugu” is unknown. The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' refers to the shrine as “Kugutsuhime Shrine” (久々都比賣神社), the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'' as “Kugu Shrine” (久具神社), and the ''{{ill|Yamato Himen Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Himen Seiki|qq=}}'' as “Kugu-sha” (久求社). Locals affectionately call it “Kugutsu Hime-san”. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}} The deities enshrined here are {{ill|Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比女命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比古命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, and {{ill|Mimae-no-Kami|ja|御前神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimae-no-Kami|qq=}}. They are regarded as the water deity—who irrigates the land of Kugu—and as a god of the five grains. This deity is identified as a child of {{ill|Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|ja|大水上命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was venerated locally as a god of water and rice cultivation even before [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto]] toured Ise. Various ancient texts such as ''{{ill|Sessessha Kokon Shidai|ja|摂末社古今次第|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sessessha Kokon Shidai|qq=}}'' confirm the names of Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto and Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, but the name of a third deity is not clearly stated.式内社研究会 編（1990）：290ページ According to tradition, these two deities appeared to greet Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto when she visited the land of Kugu. In ''{{ill|Daijingu Gishikikai|ja|大神宮儀式解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijingu Gishikikai|qq=}}'', the third deity is interpreted as the deity of the former shrine (i.e., Mimae-no-Kami), and the ''{{ill|Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|ja|神三郡神社参詣記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|qq=}}'' refers to it as “Yamajin” (mountain god). == History == According to tradition, when Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto traveled down the {{ill|Ichinose River|ja|一之瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinose River|qq=}}, she was met by Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, and Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto declared that the land was “Kugu Kono,” leading Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto to establish “Kugu-sha”. More definitively, by the definition of subsidiary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, the creation of this shrine must have occurred before the establishment of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in the 5th year of the {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} era (927 AD).伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：22ページ It is also recorded in the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=}}'', indicating that it existed before the 23rd year of the [[:en:Enryaku|Enryaku]] era (804 AD). The ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'' stipulates that if the shrine is destroyed, it should be rebuilt with proper taxation, and the ''Daijingu Shiki'' states that the shrine priest ({{ill|guji|ja|宮司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guji|qq=}}) is responsible for its repair. Furthermore, according to the ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'', there were once three main shrine buildings (正殿三宇) arranged side by side. During the medieval period, the shrine buildings fell into disrepair and even the shrine grounds became unidentifiable. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Kanbun (era)|Kanbun]] era, on September 8 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: October 8, 1663), the great shrine priest {{ill|Kawabe Seichō|ja|河邊精長|lt=Kawabe Seichō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Seichō|qq=}} (also known as Ōnakomi Seichō) made efforts to restore the shrine grounds, and on December 12 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: January 10, 1664) the relocation ceremony (遷御) was conducted. At that time, the three shrine buildings that had existed in ancient times were consolidated into one. Later, on October 7 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: November 14, 1692) the shrine building was reconstructed, and the relocation ceremony was carried out on February 18 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: March 13, 1694). According to the ''式内社調査報告'', the restored shrine grounds are undoubtedly the original site. The shrine building was rebuilt in September 1917 (Taishō 6)宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：11ページ and again in November 1955 (Shōwa 30), and a major repair was carried out in May 1979 (Shōwa 54). == Rites == In February, the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinensai]] is held; in June and December, the {{ill|Getsusai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Getsusai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} is performed; in October, the [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]] is conducted; and in November, the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]] is held in front of the shrine building, while the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January) is observed with remote worship at the Gojōden of the Imperial Grand Shrine.式内社研究会 編（1990）：291ページ A local custom called “Gosaimairi” (御祭まいり) is also practiced.櫻井（1991）：294ページ This involves many residents visiting the shrine on Lunisolar June 17 and Lunisolar September 17 (the original date of the Kannamesai before the calendar reform). == 植物相 == According to a survey conducted in 1980 (Shōwa 55), the major trees on the grounds are [[:en:Cryptomeria|Sugi]], [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], and [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Kusunoki]], while the smaller trees consist of {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=evergreen broadleaf trees|ja|常緑広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}} and {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=deciduous broadleaf trees|ja|落葉広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=}}. Moss grows along the [[:en:Sandō|sandō]]. == 上久具の渡しと久具都比売橋 == To the east of {{ill|Kugutsuhime Shrine|ja|久具都比賣神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime Shrine|qq=}}, there is the site of a ferry known as “Kamikugu no Watashi” (上久具の渡し) which operated for approximately 90 years.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：70 - 71ページ The Kamikugu ferry connected Kamikugu on both banks of the Miyagawa (upper Kugu) and Tanahashi until March 1994 (Heisei 6), facilitating the movement of people and goods.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71 - 72ページ In 1994 (Heisei 6), the construction of the Kugutsuhime Bridge resulted in the termination of the Kamikugu ferry service, which had been the last operating ferry in Mie Prefecture. Due to frequent fluctuations in the river’s water level, the Kamikugu ferry often caused difficulties for its users. As of 2013 (Heisei 25), clear remnants of the ferry landing remain on the Kamikugu side, and traces of a staircase serving as a school route can also be seen on the opposite Tanahashi side. == 交通 == ;公共交通 * From the South Exit of [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise City Station]] (JR side) on the [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangu Line]] of [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR (Tokai Passenger Railway)]], or the [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]] of [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]], take the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] route bus bound for either {{ill|Shimesasu|ja|注連指|lt=Shimesasu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimesasu|qq=}} or {{ill|Uedaguchi|ja|上田口|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uedaguchi|qq=}}, ride for approximately 30 minutes, alight at the {{ill|Dōkai Housing Complex|ja|度会団地前|lt=Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=}} bus stop, then walk for about 5 minutes.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kankomie.or.jp/spot/detail_8513.html |title=久具都比売神社（くぐつひめじんじゃ）の観光施設・周辺情報 - 観光三重 |publisher=三重県観光連盟 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-07 |accessdate=2013-11-25}} The bus runs roughly once per hour.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71ページ ;自家用車 * From [[:en:Ise Expressway|Ise Expressway]] at {{ill|Tamakishima Interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|lt=Tamakishima IC|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamakishima Interchange|qq=}}, head south on {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|ja|三重県道65号度会玉城線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|qq=}} (Sunny Road) for about 10 minutes. * From [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise City Station]], via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|ja|三重県道38号伊勢大宮線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|qq=}}, approximately 12.5 [[:en:Kilometre|km]]. {{神社 |名称= 久具都比賣神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=[[File:Kugutsuhime-jinja.jpg|270px]] |所在地 = [[三重県]][[度会郡]][[度会町]]上久具[[小字|字]]久具都裏211 |緯度度 = 34 | 緯度分 = 25 | 緯度秒 = 57.7 |経度度 = 136 |経度分 = 36 | 経度秒 = 44.9 |地図= Japan Mie |祭神= 久具都比女命
久具都比古命
御前神 |社格= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}}（小）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}摂社 |創建= [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿= [[神明造]] |別名= クグツヒメさん |札所等= |例祭= |神事= [[神嘗祭]] }} '''Kugutsuhime Shrine''' (久具都比賣神社) is a {{ill|sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sessha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 摂末社}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ([[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]) (Inner Shrine). It was established by [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]]{{ill|Ise Culture Publishing|ja|伊勢文化舎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Culture Publishing|qq=}} (2008): p.72{{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to Gakken}} (2013): p.66. The shrine is located along the [[Miya River (Mie)]] and part of the shrine grounds is occasionally subject to flooding{{ill|Shikinaisha Research Association|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft研究会|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha Research Association|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (1990): p.289. == Overview == [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]] [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Tōai District]] [[:en:Watarai|Tōai Town]] Kamikugu, in the small area ({{ill|koaza|ja|小字|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/koaza|qq=}}) of Kugutsu-uraji, is the location of this shrine. It is the only shrine affiliated with the 【神宮摂社】 (Shingū Sessha) in Tōai Town.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |title=伊勢神宮御萱場と一之瀬川流域めぐり旅 |publisher=度会町役場総務課行政係・財政係 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-19 |accessdate=2013-11-25 |archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1125-2141-54/www.town.watarai.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?frmId=909 |archivedate=2013-11-25}} Among the facilities related to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]], besides Kugutsuhime Shrine, there is also the Shingū Mikayaba located at the river’s mouth. It is Ranked 21st among the 27 subsidiary shrines (摂社) of the inner shrine.宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：9 - 11ページ The {{ill|shaden|ja|社殿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shaden|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築}} is constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style with a {{ill|itafuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/itafuki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺}} roof, and is enclosed by a single layer of [[:en:Tamagaki|tamagaki]].式内社研究会 編（1990）：292ページ Its dimensions are approximately 6 shaku wide (≒1.82 m), 4 shaku deep (≒1.21 m), and 7 shaku 8 sun high (≒2.36 m). The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,004 [[:en:Square metre|m²]]. The northern side of the shrine grounds adjoins the [[:en:Miyagawa|Miyagawa]]. When the river swells, the area around the shrine may be flooded. == 社名 == The name “Kugu” (久具) is believed to be derived from a 【地名】 (place name), although the origin of the place name “Kugu” is unknown. The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' refers to the shrine as “Kugutsuhime Shrine” (久々都比賣神社), the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延暦儀式帳}}'' as “Kugu Shrine” (久具神社), and the ''{{ill|Yamato Himen Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Himen Seiki|qq=}}'' as “Kugu-sha” (久求社). Locals affectionately call it “Kugutsu Hime-san”. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}} The deities enshrined here are {{ill|Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比女命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|久具都比古命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Mimae-no-Kami|ja|御前神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimae-no-Kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. They are regarded as the water deity—who irrigates the land of Kugu—and as a god of the five grains. This deity is identified as a child of {{ill|Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|ja|大水上命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōminakami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, who was venerated locally as a god of water and rice cultivation even before [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto]] toured Ise. Various ancient texts such as ''{{ill|Sessessha Kokon Shidai|ja|摂末社古今次第|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sessessha Kokon Shidai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' confirm the names of Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto and Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, but the name of a third deity is not clearly stated.式内社研究会 編（1990）：290ページ According to tradition, these two deities appeared to greet Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto when she visited the land of Kugu. In ''{{ill|Daijingu Gishikikai|ja|大神宮儀式解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijingu Gishikikai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', the third deity is interpreted as the deity of the former shrine (i.e., Mimae-no-Kami), and the ''{{ill|Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|ja|神三郡神社参詣記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shin Sangunjinja Sankēki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' refers to it as “Yamajin” (mountain god). == History == According to tradition, when Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto traveled down the {{ill|Ichinose River|ja|一之瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinose River|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, she was met by Kugutsuhiko-no-Mikoto, and Kugutsuhime-no-Mikoto declared that the land was “Kugu Kono,” leading Yamato Hime-no-Mikoto to establish “Kugu-sha”. More definitively, by the definition of subsidiary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, the creation of this shrine must have occurred before the establishment of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in the 5th year of the {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} era (927 AD).伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：22ページ It is also recorded in the ''{{ill|Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtaishingū Gishikichō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延暦儀式帳}}'', indicating that it existed before the 23rd year of the [[:en:Enryaku|Enryaku]] era (804 AD). The ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'' stipulates that if the shrine is destroyed, it should be rebuilt with proper taxation, and the ''Daijingu Shiki'' states that the shrine priest ({{ill|guji|ja|宮司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guji|qq=}}) is responsible for its repair. Furthermore, according to the ''Kōtaishingū Gishikichō'', there were once three main shrine buildings (正殿三宇) arranged side by side. During the medieval period, the shrine buildings fell into disrepair and even the shrine grounds became unidentifiable. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Kanbun (era)|Kanbun]] era, on September 8 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: October 8, 1663), the great shrine priest {{ill|Kawabe Seichō|ja|河邊精長|lt=Kawabe Seichō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Seichō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (also known as Ōnakomi Seichō) made efforts to restore the shrine grounds, and on December 12 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: January 10, 1664) the relocation ceremony (遷御) was conducted. At that time, the three shrine buildings that had existed in ancient times were consolidated into one. Later, on October 7 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: November 14, 1692) the shrine building was reconstructed, and the relocation ceremony was carried out on February 18 (old calendar) ([[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]: March 13, 1694). According to the ''式内社調査報告'', the restored shrine grounds are undoubtedly the original site. The shrine building was rebuilt in September 1917 (Taishō 6)宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：11ページ and again in November 1955 (Shōwa 30), and a major repair was carried out in May 1979 (Shōwa 54). == Rites == In February, the [[:en:Kinen-sai|Kinensai]] is held; in June and December, the {{ill|Getsusai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Getsusai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} is performed; in October, the [[:en:Kannamesai Festival|Kannamesai]] is conducted; and in November, the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]] is held in front of the shrine building, while the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January) is observed with remote worship at the Gojōden of the Imperial Grand Shrine.式内社研究会 編（1990）：291ページ A local custom called “Gosaimairi” (御祭まいり) is also practiced.櫻井（1991）：294ページ This involves many residents visiting the shrine on Lunisolar June 17 and Lunisolar September 17 (the original date of the Kannamesai before the calendar reform). == 植物相 == According to a survey conducted in 1980 (Shōwa 55), the major trees on the grounds are [[:en:Cryptomeria|Sugi]], [[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Chamaecyparis obtusa]], and [[:en:Camphora officinarum|Kusunoki]], while the smaller trees consist of {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=evergreen broadleaf trees|ja|常緑広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 広葉樹}} and {{ill|Broad-leaved tree|lt=deciduous broadleaf trees|ja|落葉広葉樹|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Broad-leaved tree|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 広葉樹}}. Moss grows along the [[:en:Sandō|sandō]]. == 上久具の渡しと久具都比売橋 == To the east of {{ill|Kugutsuhime Shrine|ja|久具都比賣神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugutsuhime Shrine|qq=}}, there is the site of a ferry known as “Kamikugu no Watashi” (上久具の渡し) which operated for approximately 90 years.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：70 - 71ページ The Kamikugu ferry connected Kamikugu on both banks of the Miyagawa (upper Kugu) and Tanahashi until March 1994 (Heisei 6), facilitating the movement of people and goods.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71 - 72ページ In 1994 (Heisei 6), the construction of the Kugutsuhime Bridge resulted in the termination of the Kamikugu ferry service, which had been the last operating ferry in Mie Prefecture. Due to frequent fluctuations in the river’s water level, the Kamikugu ferry often caused difficulties for its users. As of 2013 (Heisei 25), clear remnants of the ferry landing remain on the Kamikugu side, and traces of a staircase serving as a school route can also be seen on the opposite Tanahashi side. == 交通 == ;公共交通 * From the South Exit of [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise City Station]] (JR side) on the [[:en:Sangū Line|Sangu Line]] of [[:en:Central Japan Railway Company|JR (Tokai Passenger Railway)]], or the [[:en:Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Yamada Line]] of [[:en:Kintetsu Railway|Kintetsu]], take the [[:en:Mie Kotsu|Mie Kōtsū]] route bus bound for either {{ill|Shimesasu|ja|注連指|lt=Shimesasu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimesasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} or {{ill|Uedaguchi|ja|上田口|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uedaguchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, ride for approximately 30 minutes, alight at the {{ill|Dōkai Housing Complex|ja|度会団地前|lt=Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōkai Housing Complex|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} bus stop, then walk for about 5 minutes.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kankomie.or.jp/spot/detail_8513.html |title=久具都比売神社（くぐつひめじんじゃ）の観光施設・周辺情報 - 観光三重 |publisher=三重県観光連盟 |language=日本語 |date=2013-05-07 |accessdate=2013-11-25}} The bus runs roughly once per hour.伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：71ページ ;自家用車 * From [[:en:Ise Expressway|Ise Expressway]] at {{ill|Tamakishima Interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|lt=Tamakishima IC|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamakishima Interchange|qq=}}, head south on {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|ja|三重県道65号度会玉城線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 65: Dōkai-Tamakishima Line|qq=}} (Sunny Road) for about 10 minutes. * From [[:en:Iseshi Station|Ise City Station]], via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|ja|三重県道38号伊勢大宮線|lt=Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Road 38: Ise-Ōmiya Line|qq=}}, approximately 12.5 [[:en:Kilometre|km]].
